title: Other cotton waste; garnetted stock

review.classification: CPC 3.0 39215 explicitly identifies garnetted stock. The target is loose cotton fibre already opened from a recognisable knitted textile, with 39214 non-garnetted cotton waste, 39217 wearable used garments and downstream spun cotton excluded. Check actual garment-cutting origin, 100% cotton composition, navy knit construction, process state and receiving specification for each study.
review.primary_evidence: Arafat and Uddin (2022), §2.1.1 and Figures 2c and 4b, distinguish the pre-consumer navy cotton knit clip and the fibre obtained from it. The reported strength and other pooled pre-consumer test results include other wastes. The paper separately studies spinning with virgin fibre. PrecisionTex confirms a commercial colour-sorted postindustrial cotton-clip-to-loose-fibre route, without proving the experimental lots or individual dye chemistry. ANDRITZ supports typical unit operations only.
review.measurement: Both language versions separate new first-release net fibre Q from post-release shipment, original-cohort service and rework. Qualify moisture and condition on the actual lot. Segregate fibre-rich filter dust and short-fibre removal from true air emissions and from input conditioning water. Measure the polymer wrapping and straps independently. Actual first non-purchased receipts and proven same-article returns are physically distinguished from acquisitions.
review.readiness: The exact garnetted fibre reference identity and 28 other inventory-row identities are unbound. Each is disclosed. The two language projections each contain 35 cards. Independent target check performed 178 checks without skips, retaining 30 missing-range warnings. Site data, actual fibre quality, provider coverage, scientific approval, formal translation review and publication remain outstanding.
review.original_native_records: The archived polyethylene film is a plastics Product flow with a Mass reference. Input and other article movements are conditional on an actually compatible film; its material identity does not bind contaminated discarded film or its treatment. The archived water-vapour flow is elementary and belongs to emissions to unspecified air. Moisture absorbed by the material does not reuse that emissions identity. The Energy property cites a different version of the same unit group from the archive’s group version. The physical meter supports the MJ/kWh conversion independently of the electricity provider and its native property. No default packaging mix, energy supplier or fibre-performance measurement is inferred.

sources.role: Original mill experiment. Sections 2.1 and 2.2 distinguish isolated illustrations from mixed experimental test and spinning results.
First-party waste sourcing, colour sorting, mechanical conversion and loose-fibre commercial application.
Equipment manufacturer context, distinct from the actual configuration at a study site.
Pinned original ILCD files for compatible material flow and physical units.

delivery_gate: Full npm run validate is required on the exact integration source.
